pr_title: Add ability to right click on map to disable spawn points
pr_body:
This PR is a second take at the task based on feedback by the core team.

This changes the storage of disabled spawns to be just an list of spawn point indexes in the Session. The only method to disable a spawn point is using the right click button. This does reduce the discoverability of this particular feature, however it should support maps with many more spawn points than slots. The interaction toggles the point, which I think is more intuitive than the original selection.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/87995906-10464500-cb34-11ea-8be4-953453d878d0.png)

This also handles the scenario where someone joins and prevents a game from starting if there are insufficient available spawns.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/87995761-bd6c8d80-cb33-11ea-86e5-c105e06a07ed.png)

Closes #18298
pr_comments:
Bug: After fiddling around with disabling/enabling spawn points, right click to disable stopped working.

Discussion: What should happen when there are no spawns available for the players (in the case when some are disabled)? In the lobby and when the game started?

@teinarss I suspect the bug you are observing is by trial/error design. This relates to your discussion point, which I did think about and tinker with quite a bit.

I am limiting the number of disabled spawn points such that the players in the lobby are able to have a spot if the game started. The problem is if a new player comes in or you add a bot the number of players exceeds the spawns, which would cause the game to crash (I observed that during testing).

If a new person joins the lobby, the game enters into a state where there are more players than available spawn points. In this case I added checks to the autostart logic to prevent auto-start, the start button is disabled and if the start game command is issued (which should be impossible since start is disabled) it sends a message that insufficient spawns are available and the game can't start. This is shown in the Dune2k lobby screenshot above.

This check also originally had an issue where you couldn't clear a disabled spawn, so I changed it so you can always enable a disabled spawn but it still caps the disabling to free spawns. I just double checked this works if all slots fill up and there are 2 disabled spawns, you can clear both and the game.
Actually I think I found the issue you were seeing. The count for enabling spawns (and all those other places) didn't factor in observers. I just pushed a commit excluding them.
Still not working at 100%, was able to make one starting location not responding anymore after doing some chaos testing.

@teinarss I did another round of testing myself and I found 2 minor issues that are hopefully what you discovered.

* I had copied the selection logic which caused the host to ignore other players spawn selections meaning you could disable a spawn that had been selected
* Players could select a disabled spawn as the disabled spawns weren't excluded from either the dropdown or map selection

The second could happen via map selection or if the dropdown is open when a spawn is disabled, the list doesn't change with spawns being toggled. It only populates the menu when it is opened.

So in addition to these, confirmations of previous behaviour:

* Disabling spawns does not override already selected player spawns
* You can only disable up to current player count
* Emptying the lobby I was able to disable all spawns
* Manually selecting spawns and removing players enabled me to disable all spawns again
* Filling the player list with 100% disabled spawns I was able to re-enable (right-click) all and then left-click select to assign to players
* Only the game host / admin can disable spawns

The last thing I noticed was that the wording still referred to Closed Slot from my original PR, which I updated to say Closed spawn to be consistent with Available spawn.

Hopefully that addresses everything.
Thanks for the reviews, I addressed the feedback and squashed it to a single commit, rebasing on `bleed`.
@teinarss I addressed those, plus spotted another in `Exts.cs` that I fixed also

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/91362862-b0cc0b00-e83e-11ea-8bcc-be2a0378bf71.png)

OK Did the new sprites for the mods.

Also did some more testing, the last couple were bug fixes introduced related to some feedback and there was a race condition where you rapidly left then right click on a spawn and before the lobby syncs it would issue the toggle spawn command allowing you to disable a chosen spawn. A very edge case but is now handled better. I put some comments on those commits explaining the changes.

I will squash everything once you guys are happy with these most recent changes.

A few thoughts from a quick test ingame:
* Disabled spawns should show a "Disabled spawn" tooltip.
* IMO the grey background on the disabled TD spawn points looks odd. Why not the original black?
* Contrast doesn't feel great between the white X and grey background on RA etc - what if we had a black stroke that matches the spawn letters?
* Its a bit awkward to have right click disable an empty spawn, but do nothing on an occupied spawn. It would be much better if right click on an occupied spawn could remove the player.
* It feels a bit odd to have no feedback when you are trying to remove more spawns than there are currently players. I wonder whether we should add the standard click sound when selecting a spawn on the minimap, and then use the click-disabled sound on failure?
* Serious bonus points if you can also identify and fix whatever is causing the spawn letters to be drawn off-center in the markers. This has mildly bugged me for years (but never quite at the level to look into it myself).

I haven't had time to look at the code yet.

1. Disabled spawn tooltip was broken by me skipping rendering the text - I have a commit that fixes that
2. Copy/paste of the sprite from the other versions. :-)

I did some more looking into your bonus question and stepped into the SpriteFont code for the TinyBold to inspect the measurements. It appears the A character ends up as 11x11 pixels, which is clearly the cause of the odd off-center behaviour. I'm not sure it is possible to ever be 100% correct with that. Instead I figured I would try making the font larger, bumping to 12 looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/91625717-0ba36500-e9ed-11ea-9491-169a3f9cbe1f.png)

The width becomes 13x14, which doesn't solve the offset, I think the visual appearance of the offset is less.
The 'B' here is 11x14, which does look slightly to the left, but that could be visually biased slightly due to the straight edge and the rounder bumps to the right.

'C' ends up as 13x15, which again is still an odd number of pixels.

But I think this looks much more centered overall:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/91625848-e82cea00-e9ed-11ea-9256-e3b5dbb8e03d.png)

I tried applying the font change to the other mods and that made it worse over there, then I realised that cnc was the only one that appears to have issues. I adjusted the artwork to 18px for the spawn circles rather than the 19px as is current in the artwork. The PR I just created adjusts the offset for the current sprites, but I can commit the artwork changes if you think that looks better:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2775804/91626609-f2ea7d80-e9f3-11ea-9040-e6d54ef4dabc.png)

The PR has an original comparison shot vs the one above with smaller circles.

Open to suggestions as to the best change here.

Since we're changing the artwork anyway, it would make sense to fix that here too. I suspect that some of the problems may be due to point-vs-pixel alignment with HiDPI rendering, which is a bit complicated and unfair to scope creep onto a newcomer!

So I think it would make sense to change the size so we can safely assume that all mods use even-sized spawn images, and then leave further fixes to a followup PR.

review_comments:
> I rebased on bleed and surprisingly there were no conflicts, which was a first. 👍

Not quite!

It wasn't an explicit conflict, but we will now also need to make a matching change in `object IAssignSpawnPointsInfo.InitializeState(MapPreview map, Session lobbyInfo)` in `MPStartLocationsInfo` above.

FWIW this expected conflict was why I was waiting for #18696 to be merged.

I was expecting to see a check here to make sure that the spawn wasn't locked to a player slot.

Test this by adding
```
LockSpawn: True
Spawn: 1
```
under `PlayerReference@Multi0:` in map.yaml for Fort Lonestar (our favorite map for exposing bugs in lobby/server PRs) or another map of your choice.

We will need a ready check here:
```csharp
if (orderManager.LocalClient.State == Session.ClientState.Ready)
	return;
```

to avoid a bug:
* Create a lobby with more spawns disabled than there are players (so the game doesn't autostart at the next step)
* Check the ready checkbox next to your name in the player list
* Right click on an enabled spawn

Expected behaviour: Nothing happens
Actual behaviour: A pair of server error messages related to setting state while ready

The check in `SelectPlayerSpawnPoint` can then be removed, and the observer part of that was wrong!
